chapters.title: Drawing the Flow
pages:
A program is a list of small steps that a computer follows one after another. Each step reads a value, changes it a little, and hands it on to the next one. Good names make those steps easy to follow when you come back to them later. When something goes wrong, reading the code aloud often shows where the mistake is.

Short functions are easier to test, because each one does a single job. The examples here are small on purpose, so that every line can be read and understood. Try changing a number in an example and see what the program prints instead. Comments explain why the code is written the way it is, not what it does.

A value that never changes can be given a name and reused wherever it is needed. Most bugs hide in the places where two pieces of code meet and disagree. Writing the test first makes you decide what the code should do before you write it. A program is a list of small steps that a computer follows one after another.
